## Who I am

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="62%"}
- London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine, Centre for the
  Mathematical Modelling of Infectious Diseases
- Real-time outbreak analysis. $R_t$, the number of new infections per
  infected person, estimated as an outbreak happens
- Delays and nowcasting. Nowcasting is estimating what has already
  happened but has not yet been reported
- Evaluation. Scoring forecasts so that teams can be compared
:::

## epiforecasts

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="46%"}
- Led by Sebastian Funk at LSHTM. I am part of it
- The cross-over with my work is real-time modelling, and evaluating it
- `EpiNow2`, `scoringutils` and `epinowcast`. The European COVID-19
  Forecast Hub from 2021, now ECDC's RespiCast
- 2020 to 2022, weekly $R_t$ estimates and forecasts to SPI-M-O, the
  UK's modelling advisory group

::: {.attribution}
[github.com/epiforecasts](https://github.com/epiforecasts) · Hub
repository created 13 January 2021, GitHub API · SPI-M-O from
`composable-grant/coapplicant_details/sam.qmd:89`
:::

::: {.column width="54%"}
- [`epinowcast`][lk-epinowcast] was the attempt at community developed
  tools. In many cases the package is too complex for anyone else to use
- A loose forum, [community.epinowcast.org][lk-forum], over 50
  researchers and public health analysts. Community >> methods or models
  alone
- A monthly seminar since May 2023, 31 so far, organised with Fanny
  Bergström and Clara Brigitta
- 🐋 Every project I have worked on has ended up with one person doing
  most of it. Here the whale is me and a subscription
